title: Commitment Escrow & Release Hedging Playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: High-level playbook that introduces a formalized 'commitment escrow' and 'release hedging' mechanism for cycle planning. The goal is to reduce mid-cycle churn and last-minute staffing shocks by converting vague commitments into graded escrowed capacity credits, defining decommit triggers, and automating hedging lanes (soft reserves, float credits, and emergency reassignments). This playbook applies to cross-functional initiatives where PMs and ENG agree on capacity vouchers that become refundable under clearly defined risk conditions.
acceptance_criteria: A documented escrow policy (roles, voucher types, refund rules) published in Confluence
Automation: capacity-credit ledger prototype that tracks voucher issuance and consumption is deployed to staging
Two pilot initiatives run in the next cycle using escrow vouchers with measured delta on scope churn and on-time delivery
Runbook for invoking a hedge lane (soft reserve -> de-scope -> redeploy) with clear owner and SLOs is approved
Dashboard showing pledge vs actual spend and a 'commitment health' signal is visible to PMs and Eng leads
notes: Trade-off: Escrow reduces panic reallocations but adds bookkeeping and cultural overhead—success depends on light-weight automation and strong incentives for PMs to declare realistic pledges.
Design decision: Use three voucher classes (soft, firm, critical) to map to different refund mechanics and approval gates.
Operational constraint: Initial pilot will tie vouchers to team-percent FTE rather than individual names to minimize hiring/HR friction.
Risk: Overuse of 'soft' vouchers could mask chronic underestimation; mitigate by limiting consecutive soft-pledge renewals and surfacing history in the dashboard.
Implementation note: Leverage existing cycle metadata API from engineering planning service (ENG-3712) to avoid duplicating team calendars.
